title: Adding an Amazon Web Services Zero Trust Gateway

blocks.text: This article provides information on adding an Amazon Web Services (AWS) Zero Trust Gateway in the Zscaler Admin Console. To learn more, see About Amazon Web Services Zero Trust Gateways.
AWS gateways are in Limited Availability. To enable this feature, contact Zscaler Support.

blocks.item: From the navigation menu, go to Zero Trust Cloud > Zero Trust Gateway > AWS.
The Add AWS Gateway window appears.
In the Add AWS Gateway window:
Name: Enter a name for the AWS gateway.

Region: Select the AWS region where you want to create the AWS gateway. You can only deploy in one region, and you cannot modify it after the AWS gateway is created. To learn more about supported regions, see Analyzing Zero Trust Gateway Details.
Availability Zone ID: Select the availability zones where you want to create the AWS gateway components. You must select a minimum of two availability zones.

Location: Enter the name of the location to be associated with the AWS gateway. This name is visible in all the policies where the location object is available. This location object is created and synced between Cloud Connector policy pages and Internet & SaaS policy pages. To learn more, see About Locations.
Location Template: Select the location template that is used for creating the location associated with the AWS gateway.

On the Accounts tab, you must provide a list of AWS accounts that are allowed to connect to the AWS gateway being created. The Zscaler service denies endpoint connection requests from AWS accounts not present in this list. If you do not configure an AWS account while adding an AWS gateway, you must edit the AWS gateway later before connecting endpoints:

Allowed Accounts: Select the AWS accounts that are permitted to connect to the AWS gateway. The AWS gateway accepts the requests originated by endpoints from the same region as the AWS gateway. The AWS accounts in this drop-down menu were previously added by onboarding them on the Partner Integrations page in the Zscaler Admin Console. To learn more about adding an AWS account, see About Amazon Web Services Accounts.

Allowed Accounts Groups: Select the AWS account groups that are permitted to connect to the AWS gateway. The AWS gateway accepts the requests originated by endpoints from the same region as the AWS gateway. The AWS account groups in this drop-down menu were previously created on the Partner Integrations page in the Zscaler Admin Console. To learn more about adding an AWS account group, see About Amazon Web Services Account Groups.

Additional AWS Accounts: If your AWS account has not been onboarded on the Partner Integrations page, enter your 12-digit AWS account ID. The AWS gateway accepts the requests originated by endpoints from the same region as the AWS gateway. You can add up to 128 AWS accounts.
On the Review tab, confirm that the information is correct and click Create.

blocks.text: The AWS gateway is created. You can use the service address to register the endpoint. To learn more, see Registering an Endpoint in Amazon Web Services.
